research.topic: floorplan-cad: RoomPlan CapturedRoom/CapturedStructure -> 2D architectural floor plan, measurements/units, SwiftUI Canvas editing, PDF/SVG/DXF export, multi-room and multi-floor (iOS 18 target, iOS 26 SDK)

facts.claim: CapturedRoom (iOS 16) exposes the arrays we draw from: walls, doors, windows, openings, objects, plus (iOS 17) floors, sections, story, and identifier/version. Nothing in the iOS 26 SDK doc JSON is marked deprecated.
facts.api:
struct CapturedRoom
var identifier: UUID
var story: Int { get }              // iOS 17
var floors: [CapturedRoom.Surface] { get }   // iOS 17
var walls: [CapturedRoom.Surface]
var doors: [CapturedRoom.Surface]
var windows: [CapturedRoom.Surface]
var openings: [CapturedRoom.Surface]
var objects: [CapturedRoom.Object]
var sections: [CapturedRoom.Section]   // iOS 17
var version: Int
func export(to: URL, exportOptions: CapturedRoom.USDExportOptions) throws
func export(to: URL, metadataURL: URL?, modelProvider: CapturedRoom.ModelProvider?, exportOptions: CapturedRoom.USDExportOptions) throws
init(from: any Decoder) throws / func encode(to: any Encoder) throws  (Codable, Sendable)
facts.notes: CapturedRoom is Codable: persist the JSON (JSONEncoder) as the source of truth for the plan editor and re-derive geometry any time.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom.Surface members (walls, doors, windows, openings, floors all use this one type). Position/size come from transform + dimensions; shape refinements from polygonCorners, curve, completedEdges; hierarchy from parentIdentifier.
facts.availability: iOS 16.0+; parentIdentifier, polygonCorners, story, Curve.center iOS 17.0+
facts.notes: Surface has NO attributes property (only Object does). Category.floor is the category of entries in CapturedRoom.floors. Curve exists for curved walls/windows: use startAngle/endAngle/radius/center to draw an arc instead of a straight segment.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom.floors[].polygonCorners (iOS 17) is the floor outline polygon and is the correct source for room area/perimeter; polygonCorners are expressed in the surface's LOCAL plane coordinates, so each corner must be transformed by that floor's transform (world = transform * SIMD4(x, y, z, 1)) before use. Walls also get polygonCorners for non-rectangular (slanted/beamed) walls; Apple: 'Floor is now represented as a rectangle during scanning and is beautified as a polygon when scanning ends.'
facts.api:
var polygonCorners: [simd_float3] { get }   // CapturedRoom.Surface
var floors: [CapturedRoom.Surface] { get }  // CapturedRoom
facts.notes: Doc abstract: 'A 2D polygon that represents nonuniform wall heights and floor shapes... describes the polygon in local plane coordinates.' Which two of the three local components carry the polygon for a floor (x,z vs x,y) is NOT documented; a forum thread ('RoomPlan: Mapping the walls to the floor', thread 786887) exists on exactly this question but Apple forums returned 403 from this network. Mitigation: compute world points with the full 4x4 transform and drop world Y (up); that works regardless of the local convention. Floor may be empty on iOS 16 data or if the scan was too short: fall back to the wall-endpoint polygon. WWDC23 10192 transcript confirms polygonCorners and curved walls.

facts.claim: Wall endpoints in plan: RoomPlan uses a right-handed Y-up world (ARKit). A surface's transform.columns.3 is its center, columns.0 is the along-width (local X) direction, columns.1 the up direction, columns.2 the normal; dimensions.x = width (length along the wall), dimensions.y = height, dimensions.z ~ 0 for surfaces. Endpoints = transform * SIMD4(±dimensions.x/2, 0, 0, 1); plan coordinates are world (x, z) with Y dropped.
facts.notes: Official docs only say transform = 'position and orientation in the scene' and dimensions = 'bounding box'. The column semantics come from community code that ships: RoomPlan-2D (denniswave, 69 stars) and RoomPlanDemo derive pointA/pointB = (∓dimensions.x/2, 0) in surface-local space, place the node at (-position.x, position.z) and rotate by -(eulerAngles.z - eulerAngles.y) where eulerAngles.y = atan2(m[2][0], m[2][2]); forum thread 707998 (summarised by search) uses center=col3, right=col0, up=col1 for the 4 corners and col2 as the wall normal. Prefer the matrix-multiply form over Euler angles (no gimbal/sign bugs). Mirror: RoomPlan-2D negates x so the plan reads correctly when viewed from above with SpriteKit's y-up; in a y-down Canvas use (x, z) directly and verify handedness on device with a known L-shaped room.

facts.claim: Doors, windows and openings are child surfaces of a wall: parentIdentifier == wall.identifier (iOS 17). They carry their own transform/dimensions (width = dimensions.x, height = dimensions.y, sill/head height from center y ± dimensions.y/2); project their two endpoints onto the parent wall segment to cut the opening. The only door-specific data is Category.door(isOpen: Bool) (whether the door was open at scan time). There is NO hinge side, swing direction, opening side, or door type in the API; Surface has no attributes and none of the CapturedRoomAttribute types describe doors.
facts.availability: door(isOpen:) iOS 16.0+; parentIdentifier and attributes iOS 17.0+
facts.notes: Architecture consequence: door swing is an EDITABLE plan attribute we own (hinge end: left/right; swing: in/out), stored in our own plan model keyed by surface identifier, with a heuristic default (see recommendations). RoomPlanDemo added a user-toggled OpenDirection enum (clockwise/counterClockwise) for exactly this reason. Do not expect iOS 26 to add it: the iOS 26 SDK doc JSON for Surface shows no new members.

facts.claim: Wall thickness is not provided by RoomPlan: surfaces are 2D planes, dimensions.z is ~0 (bounding box of a plane). Any thickness on the plan is our rendering/CAD choice.
facts.api: var dimensions: simd_float3 { get }   // x=width, y=height, z≈0 for Surface
facts.notes: Community confirms z=0 for walls and that a downstream importer 'records a 0.001 m default plus a provenance record' (officeadmin-building-model issue #88); it-jim blog notes RoomPlan splits walls thicker than ~50 cm into two thin walls and that the USDZ 'parametric' export draws all walls at a uniform ~16 cm slab. Strategy: (1) single room: default 115 mm (4.5 in) interior / 150 mm exterior, flag 'estimated'; (2) CapturedStructure: for each wall find a wall in another room that is antiparallel (dot(normal_a, normal_b) < -0.95), overlapping in plan projection, and within 0.05-0.5 m: thickness = perpendicular distance between the two planes, flag 'measured'; keep the room-side face as the true face and offset outward by thickness so room areas stay exact.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom.Section (iOS 17) gives room-type labels with a 3D center point and story: use it to place the room name label on the plan; multiple sections may exist in one large room (e.g. kitchen + diningRoom).
facts.notes: Only 5 real labels; expect .unidentified often. Label text must be user-editable. CapturedStructure.sections aggregates all rooms' sections.

facts.claim: CapturedRoom.Object gives furniture/fixtures as oriented bounding boxes (transform + dimensions) for plan symbols; footprint = dimensions.x by dimensions.z rotated by the transform's yaw; Category.stairs exists (the only stair-related API in RoomPlan).
facts.api:
struct CapturedRoom.Object
var identifier: UUID; var parentIdentifier: UUID?  // iOS 17
var category: CapturedRoom.Object.Category
var confidence: CapturedRoom.Confidence
var transform: simd_float4x4; var dimensions: simd_float3
var story: Int  // iOS 17
var attributes: [any CapturedRoomAttribute]  // iOS 17
func attribute<T>(of: T.Type) -> T?
enum CapturedRoom.Object.Category { case bathtub, bed, chair, dishwasher, fireplace, oven, refrigerator, sink, sofa, stairs, storage, stove, table, television, toilet, washerDryer }
facts.notes: RoomPlan-2D draws objects as a rect of (dimensions.x, dimensions.z) centered at (-position.x, position.z) rotated by the same yaw formula as walls. Map categories to standard plan symbols (toilet, sink, tub, bed, stairs with direction arrow = user-set).

facts.claim: Multi-room: StructureBuilder.capturedStructure(from:) (iOS 17) merges [CapturedRoom] into a CapturedStructure whose rooms/walls/doors/windows/openings/objects/floors/sections are all in ONE shared world coordinate space. It succeeds only if the rooms 'share compatible world space': either the same ARSession was kept alive between rooms (RoomCaptureSession.stop(pauseARSession: false), then run(configuration:) again on the same session) or a new session was relocalized against a saved ARWorldMap (RoomCaptureSession(arSession:) with ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.initialWorldMap). Otherwise it throws StructureBuilder.BuildError.
facts.api:
class StructureBuilder
init(options: StructureBuilder.ConfigurationOptions)   // typealias ConfigurationOptions = RoomBuilder.ConfigurationOptions; options: [.beautifyObjects] or []
func capturedStructure(from rooms: [CapturedRoom]) async throws -> CapturedStructure
enum StructureBuilder.BuildError { case deviceNotSupported, exceedSceneSizeLimit, insufficientInput, internalError, invalidInput, invalidRoomLocation; var errorDescription: String? }
struct CapturedStructure  // Codable, Sendable
var identifier: UUID; var rooms: [CapturedRoom]
var walls, doors, windows, openings, floors: [CapturedStructure.Surface]   // typealias Surface = CapturedRoom.Surface
var objects: [CapturedStructure.Object]; var sections: [CapturedStructure.Section]; var version: Int
func export(to url: URL, metadataURL: URL? = nil, modelProvider: CapturedStructure.ModelProvider? = nil, exportOptions: CapturedStructure.USDExportOptions = .mesh) throws
// session side:
class RoomCaptureSession { init(arSession: ARSession? = nil) /* iOS 17 */; var arSession: ARSession { get }; func run(configuration: RoomCaptureSession.Configuration); func stop(); func stop(pauseARSession: Bool = true) /* iOS 17 */ }
RoomCaptureView: init(frame: CGRect, arSession: ARSession); var captureSession: RoomCaptureSession!
facts.availability: iOS 17.0+ (StructureBuilder, CapturedStructure, stop(pauseARSession:), init(arSession:)); RoomCaptureSession/RoomBuilder iOS 16.0+
facts.notes: Apple: 'Scanned structures support rooms with varying floor heights and rooms that reside on different floors in the building.' WWDC23: MultiRoom 'works best for single-floor residential houses' (1-4 bedrooms). Rooms scanned in separate app launches WITHOUT a world map are in unrelated frames: the builder will throw (invalidRoomLocation/invalidInput), so the manual drag/rotate alignment UI is required as the fallback, and our plan model must store a per-room rigid 2D transform (translation + yaw) on top of the captured data. exceedSceneSizeLimit exists: cap structure size (Apple does not publish the number).

facts.claim: Multi-floor: RoomPlan's only story support is the Int `story` on CapturedRoom, Surface, Object and Section (iOS 17) plus the CapturedStructure statement that rooms on different floors are supported. There is no stair-connection, level-height, or floor-grouping API; stairs are just Object.Category.stairs bounding boxes.
facts.api: var story: Int { get }   // CapturedRoom, CapturedRoom.Surface, CapturedRoom.Object, CapturedRoom.Section
facts.notes: How `story` is assigned (by StructureBuilder from floor elevation?) is undocumented; treat it as a hint. Robust approach: group rooms by floor surface world Y (cluster with ~1.2 m gap), let the user rename/reorder levels, and render one plan page per level; draw a stairs symbol (parallel treads + 'UP' arrow, user-set direction) from the stairs object footprint and place a matching 'DN' on the level above by same plan XY.

facts.claim: USDZ export options for the 3D outputs: .parametric (boxes/planes), .mesh (default), .model (uses ModelProvider to substitute 3D models per object category/attributes).
facts.api:
struct CapturedRoom.USDExportOptions { static let parametric, mesh, model: CapturedRoom.USDExportOptions; init(rawValue: Int32) }
struct CapturedRoom.ModelProvider { init(); var modelFileURLs: [URL]; func setModelFileURL(URL?, for: CapturedRoom.Object.Category) throws; func setModelFileURL(URL?, for: [any CapturedRoomAttribute]) throws }
facts.notes: Not floor-plan specific; listed because the 'clean architectural model' output can be the .parametric USDZ.

facts.claim: Room metrics from the data: area = shoelace over the floor polygon in plan (world x,z); perimeter = sum of polygon edge lengths; wall area = dimensions.x * dimensions.y minus child door/window areas (dimensions.x*dimensions.y of children whose parentIdentifier matches); ceiling height = median of walls' dimensions.y (walls have polygonCorners when height is non-uniform; use max corner y - min corner y in that case). All RoomPlan lengths are meters (ARKit units).
facts.api:
// shoelace
var a: Float = 0; for i in pts.indices { let p = pts[i], q = pts[(i+1) % pts.count]; a += p.x*q.y - q.x*p.y }; area = abs(a)/2
facts.availability: iOS 17.0+ for floors polygon; walls iOS 16
facts.notes: Meters as unit is the ARKit convention (verified by every community project scaling meters by a pixel factor); Apple docs do not state units explicitly on the dimensions page.

facts.claim: Foundation can format a single length with locale-aware units but CANNOT produce architectural feet-inches with fractions (12' 7 3/8"): Measurement.FormatStyle / MeasurementFormatter have unit width and usage options only; the only mixed ft+in output is the .personHeight usage (whole inches, person-height context). A custom formatter is required for imperial architectural output; use Foundation for metric and unit conversion.
facts.availability: Measurement/MeasurementFormatter iOS 10+; FormatStyle iOS 15+; Locale.MeasurementSystem iOS 16+
facts.notes: Custom imperial formatter: totalInches = meters * 39.37007874; feet = floor(totalInches/12); rem = totalInches - feet*12; round rem to nearest 1/8 (or 1/16) as numerator/denominator reduced by gcd; carry 12 in -> +1 ft; output "12' 7 3/8\"" (use ′ ″ or ' " per user setting); area in sq ft with 1 decimal. Metric: mm for < 1 m on dimension lines, m with 2 decimals otherwise, m² with 2 decimals; use Measurement(value:unit:).formatted(.measurement(width: .abbreviated, usage: .asProvided, numberFormatStyle: .number.precision(.fractionLength(2)))). Use Locale.current.measurementSystem for the default.

facts.claim: SwiftUI Canvas + GraphicsContext (iOS 15) is the right on-screen renderer for an editable plan: immediate-mode drawing of Paths, text and symbols with transforms, and withCGContext gives a CGContext so the SAME drawing routine can render into a PDF/image context.
facts.notes: GraphicsContext is a value type: copy it (var c = context) before clipping/transforming a sub-drawing. Canvas is not hit-testable per element: hit-testing must be done in our model space (distance from touch point to wall segment, etc.). Note Path.addArc's clockwise flag is interpreted in SwiftUI's y-down space (visually inverted vs. math convention).

facts.claim: Gestures for editing: DragGesture (drag walls/openings/rooms), MagnifyGesture and RotateGesture (iOS 17 replacements; MagnificationGesture/RotationGesture are marked deprecated in the doc JSON at 27.2 but still compile), SpatialTapGesture for selection with a location, @GestureState for transient offsets, .gesture/.simultaneousGesture to combine pan+pinch.
facts.api:
struct DragGesture { init(minimumDistance: CGFloat = 10, coordinateSpace: some CoordinateSpaceProtocol = .local) }  // Value: startLocation, location, translation, predictedEndLocation, velocity
struct MagnifyGesture { init(minimumScaleDelta: CGFloat = 0.01) }   // iOS 17; Value.magnification, .startAnchor
struct RotateGesture { init(minimumAngleDelta: Angle = .degrees(1)) } // iOS 17; Value.rotation
struct SpatialTapGesture { init(count: Int = 1, coordinateSpace: some CoordinateSpaceProtocol = .local) } // Value.location
@propertyWrapper struct GestureState<Value>
func gesture<T>(_ gesture: T, including mask: GestureMask = .all) -> some View
func simultaneousGesture<T>(_ gesture: T, including mask: GestureMask = .all) -> some View
facts.notes: Default parameter values shown for DragGesture/SpatialTapGesture are from memory (marked likely); the type/label names are verified. Snapping: when dragging a wall endpoint, snap to other endpoints within 0.05 m, to 0/90/45 degrees relative to neighbouring walls, and to a grid (100 mm or 1 in); wall drags move the segment along its normal keeping neighbours connected (classic 'push-pull' editing). Keep the model in meters; convert to points with a single scale/offset transform stored in view state (pinch = scale about anchor, pan = offset).

facts.claim: Vector PDF export at scale: UIGraphicsPDFRenderer (iOS 10) writes multi-page vector PDF from CGContext drawing (Path/CGPath strokes stay vector; text via NSAttributedString.draw(at:) or CoreText); page size in points (72 pt/in). For 1/4" = 1' the plan scale factor is 1:48, so points-per-meter = 39.3701 * 72 / 48 = 59.055. Alternatively CGContext(consumer:mediaBox:_:) + beginPDFPage/endPDFPage/closePDF. ImageRenderer (iOS 16) can render a SwiftUI view (incl. a Canvas) into a CGContext for PDF too, but rasterizes some content; prefer drawing directly.
facts.availability: UIGraphicsPDFRenderer iOS 10+; ImageRenderer iOS 16+; PDFKit iOS 11+
facts.notes: UIKit PDF context is y-down (UIGraphicsPDFRenderer flips for you); CGContext PDF created directly is y-up (PDF space): flip with translateBy/scaleBy(1,-1) if you share code. Letter 612x792 pt, Tabloid 792x1224, A4 595x842, A3 842x1191: auto-pick sheet + scale (1/4"=1', 1/8"=1', 1:50, 1:100) so the plan fits inside margins; print title block, scale text, north arrow, scale bar. The bottom-right title block, room schedule (name, area, ceiling height) and a dimension summary are plain text drawn at fixed page positions.

facts.claim: There is no Apple API to write SVG or DXF: both are plain-text formats we generate with string building. UTType has .pdf, .svg, .usdz; DXF needs UTType(filenameExtension: "dxf") (dynamic type) or an exported UTType declared in Info.plist (UTExportedTypeDeclarations) for a proper icon/share. Sharing: ShareLink (iOS 16) with a file URL, or fileExporter(isPresented:item:contentTypes:...) (iOS 17, Transferable). FileDocument/fileExporter(document:) are marked deprecated at 27.2 in the doc JSON (replacement: new `Document` protocol, iOS 27) but still compile on the iOS 26 SDK.
facts.api:
static var pdf: UTType { get }; static var svg: UTType { get }; static var usdz: UTType { get }
init?(filenameExtension: String, conformingTo supertype: UTType = .data)
init(exportedAs identifier: String, conformingTo parentType: UTType? = nil)
struct ShareLink<Data, PreviewImage, PreviewIcon, Label>: init<I>(item: I, subject: Text?, message: Text?, preview: SharePreview<PreviewImage, PreviewIcon>) ... (item: URL works since URL is Transferable)
nonisolated func fileExporter<T>(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, item: T?, contentTypes: [UTType] = [], defaultFilename: String? = nil, onCompletion: @escaping (Result<URL, any Error>) -> Void, onCancellation: @escaping () -> Void = { }) -> some View where T : Transferable   // iOS 17
nonisolated func fileExporter<D>(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, document: D?, contentType: UTType, defaultFilename: String? = nil, onCompletion: @escaping (Result<URL, any Error>) -> Void) -> some View where D : FileDocument   // iOS 14, deprecatedAt 27.2
facts.availability: UTType iOS 14+; ShareLink iOS 16+; Transferable fileExporter iOS 17+
facts.notes: Simplest robust path: write files into FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory (or Documents/Exports for the Files app; set UIFileSharingEnabled + LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace in Info.plist) and hand URLs to ShareLink(items: [URL]). SVG: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="..mm" height="..mm" viewBox="0 0 W H"> with 1 user unit = 1 mm; walls as <path> with stroke-width = thickness (or filled polygons), doors as <path d="M.. A r r 0 0 1 .."/>, text as <text>; group layers with <g id="walls">.

facts.claim: Minimal DXF that CAD tools import: use DXF R12 ("$ACADVER" = "AC1009"), which requires only a HEADER (optional) + ENTITIES section, no TABLES/handles/subclass markers, and supports LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, TEXT and POLYLINE+VERTEX+SEQEND entities on named layers (group 8). A hand-written R12 file with $ACADVER, $INSUNITS=6, LINE, ARC, TEXT and a POLYLINE loads in ezdxf 1.4.4 with 0 audit errors. R2000 (AC1015) LWPOLYLINE requires the 100/AcDbEntity and 100/AcDbPolyline subclass markers and handles (group 5) or it is rejected ('missing AcDbPolyline subclass').
facts.api:
$ACADVER map: AC1009=R12, AC1014=R14, AC1015=R2000, AC1018=R2004, AC1021=R2007, AC1024=R2010, AC1027=R2013, AC1032=R2018
$INSUNITS (group 70): 0 unitless, 1 inches, 2 feet, 4 millimeters, 5 centimeters, 6 meters
File skeleton (one value per line, group code then value):
0/SECTION 2/HEADER 9/$ACADVER 1/AC1009 9/$INSUNITS 70/6 0/ENDSEC
0/SECTION 2/ENTITIES
  0/LINE 8/WALLS 10/x1 20/y1 30/0 11/x2 21/y2 31/0
  0/ARC 8/DOORS 10/cx 20/cy 30/0 40/r 50/startDeg 51/endDeg   (CCW, degrees)
  0/TEXT 8/TEXT 10/x 20/y 30/0 40/height 1/string   (optional 50/rotationDeg)
  0/POLYLINE 8/WALLS 66/1 70/1(closed)|0  then 0/VERTEX 8/WALLS 10/x 20/y 30/0 ... 0/SEQEND
0/ENDSEC 0/EOF
facts.notes: Verified locally with ezdxf 1.4.4 (Python) in this session: hand_r12.dxf -> loaded AC1009, $INSUNITS read back = 6, entities [LINE, ARC, TEXT, POLYLINE], audit 0 errors/0 fixes; R2000 minimal (HEADER+ENTITIES only, with 5/handle and 100/subclass markers) also loaded with 0 audit errors, but without markers it fails. ezdxf's docs say R13+ officially also needs CLASSES/TABLES/BLOCKS/OBJECTS with LTYPE/LAYER/STYLE/APPID/DIMSTYLE/BLOCK_RECORD entries, so stick with R12 for a hand writer: AutoCAD, LibreCAD (native DXF), FreeCAD, QCAD, SketchUp Pro all read R12. $INSUNITS is not part of the R12 spec (ezdxf refuses to export it for R12 but reads it); write coordinates in millimeters or inches and ALSO state the unit in a TEXT note and the filename (plan_mm.dxf) so importers that ignore $INSUNITS still work. Use layers A-WALL, A-DOOR, A-GLAZ (windows), A-FLOR-IDEN (room names), A-ANNO-DIMS (dimension lines drawn as LINE + TEXT, not DIMENSION entities, which need DIMSTYLE tables). No Swift DXF writer exists in Apple frameworks; a ~150-line String builder is enough. Use String(format: "%.4f") with a fixed en_US_POSIX locale for numbers.

facts.claim: Community floor-plan projects and their drawing conventions: RoomPlan-2D (denniswave, 69 stars, SpriteKit, 2023) and its descendant RoomPlanDemo (BaidetskyiYurii, 2025, SpriteKit+SwiftUI, PNG/JPEG/PDF export via UIGraphicsPDFRenderer + UIActivityViewController, tap-to-inspect, editable door open direction, annotations, iOS 16). Both: scale meters by a constant (200 px/m), walls = thick stroked line between (∓dimensions.x/2, 0) in surface-local space, doors = background-colored line over the wall gap + a door leaf line rotated 45° from the hinge end + a dashed quarter-circle arc (radius = door width) around the hinge end, windows = thin line (RoomPlanDemo mistakenly also draws an arc for windows), openings = just the gap, objects = rotated rect (dimensions.x by dimensions.z) with 30% fill.
facts.notes: Neither project draws dimension lines, room labels, north arrow or scale bar; none writes SVG/DXF; none handles multi-room or wall thickness. Other repos found: Tupham16/CedarScan (CubiCasa-style, has OBJ/GLB exporters), codeyu/roomplan-2d-viewer (fork of RoomPlan-2D), zuls/roomplan (2D&3D). The it-jim blog and Apple ML page are useful background; totheroot.io articles (Parts I/II) are JS-rendered and unreadable by fetch, but their code is the RoomPlan-2D repo.

facts.claim: Standard architectural plan symbol conventions to implement: swing door = gap in wall + leaf line perpendicular (or 90° open) from hinge + quarter-circle arc (radius = leaf width) from leaf tip to strike jamb, thin dashed or thin solid; window = wall outline with a thin line (or 2-3 parallel lines: 'triple line' for glazing) across the gap; opening/cased opening = gap with dashed line across; dimension lines = thin line offset ~0.6-1 m from the wall face with extension lines from the measured points, 45° tick marks (architectural) or arrowheads (engineering), text centred above the line reading left-to-right or bottom-to-top; overall exterior dimension string outside the inner string; room tag = NAME (uppercase) with area beneath; north arrow top-right; graphic scale bar (0-5-10 ft or 0-1-2-5 m) near the title block; wall line weight heaviest (walls cut in section), then fixtures, then dimensions/annotations lightest.
facts.notes: Conventions from general architectural drafting practice (US AIA/NCS style); the linked tutorial covers door/arc drawing. Stairs: parallel tread lines at ~280 mm spacing, a centreline with arrow and 'UP'/'DN', break line across the flight at the cut plane. Since RoomPlan gives no door swing, render the plan in a 'sketch' style until the user confirms swings, or use a heuristic default.

gotchas: polygonCorners are LOCAL to the surface plane: multiply by the surface transform before use; which local axes carry the polygon (x,z for floors?) is undocumented, so always go through the full 4x4 and drop world Y.

Curved walls: Surface.curve != nil; the wall is an arc (center in local xz, radius, start/end angles as Measurement<UnitAngle>); a straight segment from ±dimensions.x/2 is wrong for these. Also curve.center is iOS 17.

Door/window endpoints computed from their own transform may sit slightly off the parent wall line (different y and small normal offset): project onto the parent wall segment (parentIdentifier) and clamp to [0, wallLength].

CapturedRoom coordinates differ per scan unless the ARSession was continued or relocalized: StructureBuilder throws instead of guessing. Persist ARWorldMap between rooms if you want cross-launch merging; otherwise offer manual alignment.

Y is up in RoomPlan/ARKit; plan uses (x, z). One axis must be mirrored depending on whether the canvas is y-down (SwiftUI) or y-up (SpriteKit/PDF CGContext) or the plan comes out mirrored. Verify handedness on device with an L-shaped room before shipping.

Wall dimensions.x is the length of the detected wall face, which often overshoots/undershoots at corners; for a clean architectural plan intersect adjacent wall lines (extend infinite lines and take the intersection when the angle is not near 0/180) rather than trusting endpoints; use the floor polygon as the authoritative room outline.

Wall thickness, door swing, hinge side, door type (sliding/pocket), stairs direction and room names beyond 5 labels are NOT in the data; all must be user-editable in our own plan model keyed by surface/object identifier.
dimensions.y of a wall may be the scanned height, not the true ceiling height if the scan missed the top; use the max over walls / median with confidence == .high.

GraphicsContext.draw(Text) uses the view's environment font; text size in a scaled canvas scales with the transform unless you draw text after resetting the transform (draw labels in screen space using converted points).
UIGraphicsPDFRenderer contexts are y-down (UIKit); a CGContext created with CGContext(consumer:mediaBox:) is y-up PDF space; do not mix without a flip.
Path.addArc(clockwise:) in SwiftUI/CoreGraphics on iOS is visually inverted relative to the math convention because y points down; test the door arc direction.

DXF: R12 has no $INSUNITS in the spec (readers may ignore it) and no LWPOLYLINE; R2000+ needs subclass markers/handles/tables. Numbers must use '.' decimal separator (use Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")).

FileDocument/fileExporter(document:) and MagnificationGesture/RotationGesture are marked deprecated (27.2) in the current doc JSON; they compile on the iOS 26 SDK but prefer ShareLink/Transferable fileExporter (iOS 17) and MagnifyGesture/RotateGesture (iOS 17).
StructureBuilder.BuildError.exceedSceneSizeLimit exists with no published limit; plan for large houses to fail to merge and fall back to per-room plans with manual placement.

Apple Developer Forums return HTTP 403 from this network (curl, WebFetch, jina proxy, and Chrome all blocked); forum-sourced details in this report come from search-engine summaries and were cross-checked against shipping GitHub code.
recommendations: Deployment target iOS 17 is the real floor for this feature (floors/polygonCorners, parentIdentifier, sections, story, StructureBuilder, MagnifyGesture/RotateGesture, Transferable fileExporter are all iOS 17); iOS 18.0 as planned is fine and nothing here needs 18. Nothing here is iOS 26-only.

Build a pure-Swift `PlanModel` (meters, plan XY = world x,z) derived once from CapturedRoom/CapturedStructure: Room { id, name, floorPolygon:[CGPoint], story, alignment: CGAffineTransform }, Wall { id, p0, p1, thicknessMM, thicknessSource(.estimated/.measured/.user), height, curve? }, Opening { id, wallId, kind(.door(swing, hinge)/.window/.opening), offsetAlongWall, width, sillHeight, headHeight }, Fixture { id, category, center, size, yaw }. Edits apply to this model (never mutate RoomPlan types); keep the CapturedRoom JSON alongside for re-derivation.

Geometry: endpoints = transform * (±w/2,0,0,1); build the room outline from floors[0].polygonCorners (transform applied) and fall back to a wall-corner polygon (intersect consecutive wall lines) when floors is empty; door/window cut = project child endpoints onto parent wall via parentIdentifier; curved walls from Surface.curve.

Door swing default heuristic (all editable): hinge = the door end closer to the nearest wall corner (doors are typically hung near a corner); swing side = into the room whose floor polygon contains doorCenter + normal*0.3 m (for single room: the scanned room); if category is .door(isOpen: true) keep the same defaults; store the user's choice per surface identifier.

Wall thickness: default 115 mm interior / 150 mm exterior (mark estimated); in CapturedStructure detect antiparallel overlapping walls within 0.05-0.5 m and use the plane distance (mark measured); draw walls as filled polygons offset outward from the room-side face so measured room areas are unchanged.

Rendering: write one `PlanRenderer.draw(model, into: CGContext, scale: pointsPerMeter, style:)` in Core Graphics and call it from SwiftUI Canvas via context.withCGContext for the screen and from UIGraphicsPDFRenderer for PDF; keep SVG and DXF as separate string writers over the same PlanModel (walls as closed POLYLINE/LWPOLYLINE-equivalent polygons on A-WALL, doors as LINE + ARC on A-DOOR, windows as 3 parallel LINEs on A-GLAZ, dimension strings as LINE+TEXT on A-ANNO-DIMS, room names/areas as TEXT on A-FLOR-IDEN, in millimeters with $INSUNITS=4 for R12).

Units: store meters; UnitsFormatter with two modes: imperial architectural (feet-inches, nearest 1/8", sq ft) via custom code, metric (mm under 1 m, m to 2 decimals, m²) via Measurement.FormatStyle; default from Locale.current.measurementSystem; user override in settings.

PDF: choose sheet (Letter/Tabloid/A4/A3) and scale (1/4"=1', 1/8"=1', 1:50, 1:100) automatically to fit; draw title block, scale text and graphic scale bar, north arrow (user-rotatable, default 'up = +z'), room schedule table; use kCGPDFContextTitle/Author in UIGraphicsPDFRendererFormat.documentInfo; one page per level.

Editing UX in Canvas: model-space hit test (segment distance < 12 pt / scale), DragGesture on selected wall moves along its normal keeping neighbours joined, endpoint handles with snapping (endpoints 50 mm, angles 0/45/90, grid 100 mm or 1 in), MagnifyGesture/DragGesture for view pan/zoom (two-finger), undo via a value-type history stack (PlanModel is a struct).

Multi-room: capture with one RoomCaptureSession and stop(pauseARSession: false) between rooms (plus save ARWorldMap for resume); merge with StructureBuilder; if merging throws, load rooms as independent PlanModel.Room entries and provide a 'Arrange rooms' mode: drag (DragGesture) + two-finger rotate (RotateGesture) per room with snapping of parallel walls (align + touch faces, gap = thickness) and shared-door snapping (door centers of two rooms coincide).

Multi-floor: group rooms by floor world Y (cluster gap ~1.2 m) and by CapturedRoom.story as a hint; one plan per level; stairs from Object.Category.stairs footprint with user-set direction; no cross-level alignment API exists, so align levels by the stair footprint and exterior walls, user-adjustable.

Testing without a Mac: add a JSON fixture of a real CapturedRoom (encode on device, pull over USB with pymobiledevice3 like the interpreter project) and unit-test the geometry/DXF/SVG writers in CI (xcodebuild test on the macOS runner) so wrong-axis bugs are caught without a device round trip; validate DXF output with `ezdxf` audit in a CI Python step.

Whether Surface.transform for walls is guaranteed to have columns.1 == world up (no roll) and whether columns.0 always points along the wall length (vs. sometimes along height): community code assumes yes; confirm on device on a wall with polygonCorners.

Whether Apple Developer sample 'MergingMultipleScansIntoASingleStructure' (zip 3e2b731b0ef7/MergingMultipleScansIntoASingleStructure.zip) contains any plan-alignment logic; not downloaded (download requires user permission).

unverified_critical_claims: CapturedRoom.floors[].polygonCorners (iOS 17) is the floor outline polygon and is the correct source for room area/perimeter; polygonCorners are expressed in the surface's LOCAL plane coordinates, so each corner must be transformed by that floor's transform (world = transform * SIMD4(x, y, z, 1)) before use. Walls also get polygonCorners for non-rectangular (slanted/beamed) walls; Apple: 'Floor is now represented as a rectangle during scanning and is beautified as a polygon when scanning ends.'

Wall endpoints in plan: RoomPlan uses a right-handed Y-up world (ARKit). A surface's transform.columns.3 is its center, columns.0 is the along-width (local X) direction, columns.1 the up direction, columns.2 the normal; dimensions.x = width (length along the wall), dimensions.y = height, dimensions.z ~ 0 for surfaces. Endpoints = transform * SIMD4(±dimensions.x/2, 0, 0, 1); plan coordinates are world (x, z) with Y dropped.

Doors, windows and openings are child surfaces of a wall: parentIdentifier == wall.identifier (iOS 17). They carry their own transform/dimensions (width = dimensions.x, height = dimensions.y, sill/head height from center y ± dimensions.y/2); project their two endpoints onto the parent wall segment to cut the opening. The only door-specific data is Category.door(isOpen: Bool) (whether the door was open at scan time). There is NO hinge side, swing direction, opening side, or door type in the API; Surface has no attributes and none of the CapturedRoomAttribute types describe doors.
Wall thickness is not provided by RoomPlan: surfaces are 2D planes, dimensions.z is ~0 (bounding box of a plane). Any thickness on the plan is our rendering/CAD choice.

Multi-room: StructureBuilder.capturedStructure(from:) (iOS 17) merges [CapturedRoom] into a CapturedStructure whose rooms/walls/doors/windows/openings/objects/floors/sections are all in ONE shared world coordinate space. It succeeds only if the rooms 'share compatible world space': either the same ARSession was kept alive between rooms (RoomCaptureSession.stop(pauseARSession: false), then run(configuration:) again on the same session) or a new session was relocalized against a saved ARWorldMap (RoomCaptureSession(arSession:) with ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.initialWorldMap). Otherwise it throws StructureBuilder.BuildError.

Foundation can format a single length with locale-aware units but CANNOT produce architectural feet-inches with fractions (12' 7 3/8"): Measurement.FormatStyle / MeasurementFormatter have unit width and usage options only; the only mixed ft+in output is the .personHeight usage (whole inches, person-height context). A custom formatter is required for imperial architectural output; use Foundation for metric and unit conversion.

Vector PDF export at scale: UIGraphicsPDFRenderer (iOS 10) writes multi-page vector PDF from CGContext drawing (Path/CGPath strokes stay vector; text via NSAttributedString.draw(at:) or CoreText); page size in points (72 pt/in). For 1/4" = 1' the plan scale factor is 1:48, so points-per-meter = 39.3701 * 72 / 48 = 59.055. Alternatively CGContext(consumer:mediaBox:_:) + beginPDFPage/endPDFPage/closePDF. ImageRenderer (iOS 16) can render a SwiftUI view (incl. a Canvas) into a CGContext for PDF too, but rasterizes some content; prefer drawing directly.

Minimal DXF that CAD tools import: use DXF R12 ("$ACADVER" = "AC1009"), which requires only a HEADER (optional) + ENTITIES section, no TABLES/handles/subclass markers, and supports LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, TEXT and POLYLINE+VERTEX+SEQEND entities on named layers (group 8). A hand-written R12 file with $ACADVER, $INSUNITS=6, LINE, ARC, TEXT and a POLYLINE loads in ezdxf 1.4.4 with 0 audit errors. R2000 (AC1015) LWPOLYLINE requires the 100/AcDbEntity and 100/AcDbPolyline subclass markers and handles (group 5) or it is rejected ('missing AcDbPolyline subclass').
